$comment: Who this project trusts, and how much. Committed to the default branch and
changed by pull request, which is what makes granting trust a reviewable act
rather than something an agent can assert about itself over the wire.
A signature that verifies against a key here reads `verified` or better.
Anything else reads `pinned` (a key we have seen before under this name) or
`unverified`. Trust is a property of the signature, never of what a record
`github` pulls whatever that account currently publishes at
https://github.com/<login>.keys, so a rotated key works with no PR here.
`keys` pins one explicitly, which is what you want offline or off-GitHub.

members.$agents: optional: list the agent names this account may sign as, e.g. ["fable-arch"]. Omitted means the github login itself is the only bound name.
